citeAs: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (2024). TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv:2402.01622.
creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI)
description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark focused on travel planning that provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet, accessible via six tools (CitySearch, FlightSearch, DistanceMatrix, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, AccommodationSearch). It contains 1,225 meticulously curated diverse user queries along with their reference plans, each imposing a different combination of constraints including environment constraints, commonsense constraints, and hard constraints (budget, room type, cuisine, transportation preferences).
name: TravelPlanner
rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (one reference plan per query, annotated by one of the 20 graduate students and verified by authors)
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 graduate students (specific institutions, nationalities, or other demographic details not provided).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed by authors reviewing every query and plan and rectifying errors. Plans were validated against an automated evaluation script that checks all constraints. Only plans meeting all constraints were accepted. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans through multiple stages of human verification. The process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation process (no specific platform mentioned; 20 graduate students annotated plans directly using the evaluation script as quality check).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Twenty graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan was deemed eligible only if it met all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 for each plan they annotated. Authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment specifically designed to avoid variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data, ensuring all agents access the same unchanging information. Restaurant data was randomly assigned to cities (not geographically accurate), and accommodation data was similarly randomly distributed. The commonsense constraints reflect the authors' consensus, which may introduce cultural or individual bias in what is considered commonsense.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset environment was constructed by sourcing data from multiple publicly available Internet sources: FlightSearch data from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (spanning 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01); DistanceMatrix data computed via the Google Distance Matrix API; RestaurantSearch data from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset; AttractionSearch data gathered via the Google Places API; AccommodationSearch data from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. Data was then modified (adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values) to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. Queries were constructed by randomly selecting departure city, destination, date range, travel duration, and hard constraints, then using GPT-4 to generate natural language queries. Reference plans were annotated by 20 graduate students.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset for flight information; (2) Google Distance Matrix API for driving distances and travel times between cities; (3) Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset for restaurant names and average costs; (4) Google Places API for attraction information (name, address, phone, website, latitude, longitude); (5) Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset for accommodation details (name, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate, maximum occupancy).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Flight data spans from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. Other data sources (restaurants, attractions, accommodations) were collected from Kaggle datasets and APIs at the time of benchmark construction.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment, which may not fully reflect the dynamic nature of real-world travel planning. The commonsense constraints are based on the authors' consensus and may not capture all possible definitions of commonsense. The dataset covers only travel planning within the US (based on the cities and states referenced). The data spans only March 2022 for flights.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Source data was modified to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination: keys and values were added, deleted, and altered. Restaurants were randomly assigned to cities and randomly categorized under cuisine types. Accommodations were randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules. Flight prices were generated by multiplying distance by a random factor (0.2–0.5). Query budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets and reduce the number of feasible plans.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For FlightSearch: extracted fields including FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, DestCityName; generated Price by multiplying Distance by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. For DistanceMatrix: calculated Price for self-driving and taxi by multiplying Distance by factors of 1 and 0.15 respectively; stored results in a fixed database. For RestaurantSearch: extracted Restaurant Name and Average Cost; randomly assigned restaurants to various cities; randomly categorized each restaurant under cuisines (Chinese, American, Italian, Mexican, Indian, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, Korean, Asian, French). For AccommodationSearch: extracted NAME, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate number, maximum occupancy; randomly assigned items to cities; assigned random room rules. Data was modified (adding, deleting, altering keys and values) to avoid data contamination.
rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research. Some data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the content does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The authors acknowledge that definitions of commonsense may differ across individuals and encourage additional discussions to enrich the commonsense dimension. Evaluation scripts will be released to foster innovation. The authors encourage use of evaluation feedback in training (e.g., reinforcement learning) but strictly prohibit cheating in validation and test sets to uphold fairness and reliability.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating language agents' capabilities in complex multi-constraint planning and tool use, specifically in travel planning scenarios. Intended as a benchmark for assessing LLM-powered agents on long-horizon planning, constraint satisfaction, tool use, and working memory management. Also intended to serve as a testbed for future research to develop more capable language agents approaching human-level planning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries from structured JSON elements. GPT-4-Turbo was used to extract key components (transportation, restaurants, attractions, accommodations) from natural language plans into structured JSON format for evaluation.
